name: CP-PACS Lattice QCD benchmark
description: The CP-PACS is a massively parallel computer dedicated for calculations in computational physics and will be in operation in the spring of 1996 at Center for Computational Physics, University of Tsukuba. In this article, we describe the architecture of the CP-PACS and report the results of the estimate of the performance of the CP-PACS for typical lattice QCD calculations.
evaluation_method: time-to-solution and sustained floating-point performance (FLOPS), together with checks on physics outputs (e.g., observable agreement) to verify correctness
general_score_metric: sustained FLOPS / time-to-solution (with physics observable agreement as a correctness metric)
reputation: Historically significant HPC benchmark in the lattice QCD and computational physics community for evaluating system performance and physics output fidelity.
notes: Platform- and implementation-sensitive HPC benchmark; performance depends strongly on hardware, compilers, and code optimizations; correctness (physics output) is as important as raw performance; not an ML/LLM benchmark.
